rationale: The candidate is readable as one compact mass with a stepped/cantilevered profile, but it is not yet a convincing neighborhood-living massing. Across the four views the form is coherent enough to avoid a total failure, yet the dominant gesture is still ambiguous: it reads as a generic prismatic block with one tapered end and a shallow notch, not as a clearly organized live/work neighborhood building. The blue access edge is not strongly answered by a public void, court, or entry seam; the ground response remains mostly sealed and semantically passive. The central/side carving is too slight to carry the required public-space role, so the void logic is weak. The silhouette has some sectional interest, but it behaves more like a stepped object than a program-bearing section. Compared with the references, the candidate only partially resonates with the courtyard/terrace language and lacks the stronger open-ground and bridging/public-threshold articulation seen in the similar precedents.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise community massing with a large central void and a bridge-like upper connector reads as a neighborhood public building with a clear spatial heart.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is larger and more campus-like than the candidate; do not copy the scale or perimeter tower language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like composition around a central court can support neighborhood living when the ground plane stays open and legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is more retail-hospitality in character and more horizontally spread than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long, calm mass with a carved central void and roof articulation can fit a compact mixed-use/public building.
Terraced, connected low-rise volumes with a public open space and sectional variation are highly transferable to neighborhood living.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More office/cultural than residential-neighborhood; use the spatial structure, not the typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a courtyard with voids under elevated blocks reinforce public threshold and hierarchy.
